source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Caplin sources ~30% of outsourced LatAm products from China; company refers to a 'China 2.0' strategy to fast-track entry into biosimilars and peptides. No explicit China+1 revenue attribution or supply-chain diversification framing directed at benefiting from China exit.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company does not enter into derivatives for hedging; debt-light with internal accrual-funded capex of INR 887 Cr over 8 years. No floating rate borrowing disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No derivative hedging contracts; relies on natural hedge given exports are USD/local currency denominated.
inr_exposure.evidence: Company does not enter into any derivatives contracts for hedging; foreign exchange earned of INR 720 crores and foreign exchange used of INR 25 crores (standalone FY25). Primary export markets are Latin America (~76% of total) and Africa (~6%), with US/regulated markets ~18%.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme participation found in FY2025 disclosures. Caplin focuses on branded generics for LatAm/Africa and US injectables, not bulk drug/API manufacturing targeted by pharma PLI.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total borrowings over INR 2,100 Cr; specific floating vs fixed breakdown not disclosed. USD-denominated loans naturally hedge USD raw material purchases.

crude_exposure.evidence: Green coffee beans (not crude oil) are primary raw material. Gross margins contracted 920 bps in Q4 FY25 due to volatile green coffee prices. Crude not a material input.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge: imports green coffee beans in USD and earns export revenues in USD; also has USD-denominated loans. Limited derivative hedging disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports approximately 90% of revenue. Operates manufacturing in India, Vietnam and Switzerland. CIS/Russia ~20-25%, Europe ~13%, North America ~13%, Middle East/Africa balance.

pli_scheme.evidence: No specific CCL PLI participation or incentive receipts found in FY2025 annual report disclosures.

govt_capex.evidence: Aegis handles LPG imports and distribution for domestic market; significant LPG volumes flow through OMC (Oil Marketing Companies) / government-linked distribution channels, but specific government capex revenue % not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Specific floating vs fixed rate borrowing breakdown not accessible from available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Gas Terminal segment (LPG/petroleum imports, storage, distribution) accounts for ~90% of FY2025 revenue (INR 61.14B out of INR 67.64B total). Purchases of LPG/petroleum products constitute the dominant cost item; Aegis is a pass-through logistics business where petroleum product cost is the primary 'raw material'.

inr_exposure.evidence: Aegis imports LPG in USD but sells domestically in INR; forex risk exists on import payables rather than revenue. Specific hedging policy not accessible from available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to LPG terminal/logistics operations.

rural.evidence: ABSLAMC has pan-India presence across 300+ locations with 10.6 million folios as of March 2025; rural/B30 AUM as a percentage of total AUM (INR 4,056 billion) not separately disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABSLAMC is debt-free; total external debt INR 0, debt-to-equity ratio 0%. No floating rate liabilities to measure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Primarily a domestic fee-based AUM business. International subsidiaries in Dubai, Mauritius, and Singapore handle offshore/NRI AUM (~5% of total AUM). No material USD revenue or hedging policy disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Asset management companies are not beneficiaries of any PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company implemented proactive logistics planning and diversified sourcing strategies; 'supply resilience via diversified raw-material sourcing (reduced China dependence)'; Unit-3 facility near Kakinada commenced commercial production strengthening backward integration. US Biosecure Act tailwinds creating new RFPs from global Big Pharma. Positioned to capture C+1 contract flow among Indian CDMO/API companies.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company historically carries low debt levels. Specific floating vs fixed rate breakdown not accessible from available sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Export revenue primarily in USD/EUR; specific hedging policy details not accessible from available sources.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue represented 88% of total sales revenue in FY2024-25. Europe and the US accounted for 73% of total sales revenue combined.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories qualifies under PLI scheme for pharmaceuticals (Category 2: APIs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates). Government PLI pharma scheme covers API manufacturers with financial incentives of INR 15,000 crore over six years on incremental sales.

china_plus_one.evidence: MD&A: 'Ongoing trade tensions, especially between the U.S. and China, as well as regional conflicts, are leading to a rethink of global supply chains. Policies like the proposed Biosecure Act in the U.S., aimed at reducing dependency on China, are prompting global pharma players to diversify suppliers and invest in regional manufacturing hubs. Lupin, with its robust India-based manufacturing and CDMO operations, is well placed to support this transition. Through API Plus and LMS, Lupin is not only ensuring secure global supply chains, but also elevating India's stature in the global API and CDMO landscape.'

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses forward contracts and options to hedge forex exposure; specific amounts not publicly confirmed.
inr_exposure.evidence: US business = 36% of global FY25 sales; EMEA ~9%; Emerging Markets ~11%; API ~5%; India 34%. Aggregate export revenue ~66% of total INR 227 Bn revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Revenue rise aided by higher PLI and export benefits per FY25 results. Lupin participates in pharma PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs; exact incentive amount not disclosed separately.

rural.evidence: VBL reaches 3.5-4 million FMCG outlets of 12 million total; deployment of 1.1 million visi-coolers; active rural penetration with 10-12% annual outlet addition target; distribution network covers urban, semi-urban, and rural markets.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt fell to Rs 8 billion from Rs 32 billion in CY23 (down 73.6%); finance costs increased 65.6% YoY from Africa/BevCo acquisition financing; specific floating rate breakdown not confirmed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Total cost of materials consumed = 41.3% of net revenue in CY2024; key materials include PET chips (crude-linked petrochemical) and sugar (not crude-linked). Specific crude-linked PET chip proportion not separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International revenues (South Africa BevCo, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Morocco, and other African geographies) contributed ~28% of net operational revenues in CY2024.

china_plus_one.evidence: Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits Navin Fluorine International's export-led business. European CDMO MSA outlook remains strong with confirmed orders and new molecule contracts. Company entered long-term supply contracts with South African miners for fluorspar to de-risk from China dependency.

crude_exposure.evidence: Fluorspar accounts for over 40% of NFIL's overall raw material cost; total raw material as % of revenue not confirmed. Fluorspar prices are highly volatile; China is the key global supplier but NFIL has diversified to South African miners.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution ~65% in FY25. CDMO segment export demand accounted for over 95% of segment revenue; primary export markets are Europe and US.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI beneficiary status confirmed for NFIL in available public disclosures.

rural.evidence: Products available in approximately 216,000 villages; 5.2 million retail outlets; relationships with over 10,000 distributors; 'RUrban' journey since 2019 with active expansion. E-commerce 8.6% of sales with 45% from Quick Commerce.

crude_exposure.evidence: Total materials consumed ~41.5% of revenue (15-month FY2024-25). Key inputs are milk, wheat, sugar, cocoa, coffee, edible oils — predominantly agricultural commodities. Crude-linked packaging is a secondary input; specific proportion not separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Predominantly domestic India revenue; minimal forex exposure; sourcing >97% locally.
inr_exposure.evidence: Nestle India has almost entirely domestic India revenue (exports <1%). CHF 2.01 billion in sales contributing 2.2% of global Nestle S.A. revenues.

govt_capex.evidence: Indirect exposure through EPCs ~35-40% of revenue. Large orders up 20% for CY2024 driven by data centers, railways, metals and mining, energy, buildings and infrastructure. Higher capex in infrastructure, railways, renewables, and power distribution providing significant growth opportunities.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Cash balance of INR 5,390 crore (14% increase YoY); company is net cash positive with minimal debt.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials include copper, steel, and electronic components. Positive material/commodity price movement contributed to margin expansion in CY2024.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for approximately 10% of business mix per Q4 2024 earnings call; exports primarily through ABB global supply chain divisions.

china_plus_one.evidence: CEO Krishna Kanumuri: 'As large pharma increasingly diversifies supply chains in a China+1 strategy, CDMOs in India are stepping into a new era of opportunity. The focus of innovator companies on diversifying their supply chains bodes well for Indian CROs-CDMOs like ours.' Sai Life Sciences is positioned as a key beneficiary of global supply-chain realignment away from China.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company repaid ₹720 Cr of debt in FY2025; balance sheet significantly deleveraged post-IPO. Specific floating vs fixed rate split not publicly disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: As a CDMO/CRO, primary inputs are chemicals and solvents for synthesis; not directly crude-linked in a material way. Specific RM as % of revenue not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contribute up to 99% of total revenues, primarily from companies in the US and Europe. Revenue billed to global innovator pharma companies denominated in USD.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sai Life Sciences is a CDMO focused on innovator/patented molecules (NCEs), not bulk API manufacturing targeted by pharma PLI. No evidence of PLI scheme beneficiary status.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is largely debt-free (ROCE 32%, RONW 25% in FY2025). Specific floating rate liability split not publicly disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: API prices softened in FY2025, benefiting gross margins. Ajanta sources APIs externally; crude not a direct input.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY2025: India domestic ₹1,452 Cr (31%), Asia branded generics ₹1,191 Cr (26%), US generics ₹1,047 Cr (23%), Africa branded generics ₹750 Cr (16%), Africa institutional ₹147 Cr (3%). Total revenue ₹4,648 Cr.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence of Ajanta Pharma being a PLI scheme beneficiary. Ajanta focuses on finished formulations (branded generics), not bulk drug/API manufacturing.

china_plus_one.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films derives 77% of revenue from exports with US as largest market. Management discussed geographic diversification strategy to reduce US market dependence amid tariff challenges, expanding to Europe, Middle East and East Africa. Analyst community identifies GHFL as a China+1 beneficiary in specialty polyester films; company has not used explicit 'China+1' framing in available FY2025 disclosures.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reached 'Debt to Zero' milestone by FY2025 — effectively debt-free.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are Purified Terephthalic Acid (PTA) and Monoethylene Glycol (MEG), both petrochemical derivatives whose prices move with crude oil. Specific RM cost as % of revenue not disclosed. EBITDA margins expanded to 20.9% in FY2025 from 16.8% in FY2024, aided by favorable RM pricing.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses forward contracts for hedging raw material procurement; specific FX hedging policy for export receivables not separately confirmed.
inr_exposure.evidence: 77% of FY2025 revenues from exports; US is the largest export market with significant USD exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence of PLI scheme participation for specialty polyester films.

rural.evidence: Royal Enfield is a premium motorcycle brand (₹1.5-3.5 lakh segment) primarily sold in urban/semi-urban markets. No specific rural revenue percentage disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: VECV (commercial vehicles JV, ~55% of consolidated revenue) has significant exposure to government infrastructure spending; bus segment captured 35% market share via government contracts. Specific government capex revenue % not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Eicher Motors is a net cash company with minimal debt; long-term debt ~₹2 billion primarily at VECV subsidiary level.

crude_exposure.evidence: Steel, aluminum, rubber, and other metals are primary raw materials. Not directly crude oil-linked.

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield FY2025: domestic 902,757 units (90%), exports 100,136 units (10%), growing 29.7% YoY. VECV exported 5,181 trucks/buses (vs 3,721 in FY24), growing 39.2%.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI scheme for automobile and auto components extended through FY28. Eicher Motors' Royal Enfield and VECV are eligible participants for advanced automotive technology manufacturing. Specific PLI incentive as % of revenue not disclosed.

rural.evidence: Tier-2/3 expansion is a stated strategic priority; company operates 298 clinical laboratories and 6,607 Patient Service Centers as of FY2025, expanding deeper into Tier-III and beyond. Targets 15-20 new labs per year. Specific rural/tier-2/3 revenue % not publicly disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) cited as supportive government initiative driving diagnostic industry growth. Specific government scheme revenue contribution not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is largely debt-free (PAT ₹492 Cr on revenue ₹2,548 Cr in FY2025; net cash position).

crude_exposure.evidence: Diagnostics company; primary costs are reagents, consumables, and employee costs. Crude oil not a direct material input.

inr_exposure.evidence: Pure domestic India diagnostics company with 100% INR revenues. FY2025 revenue ₹2,548 Cr, all from Indian patients.

pli_scheme.evidence: Diagnostics services company; PLI schemes cover manufacturing sectors, not healthcare services.

govt_capex.evidence: Clients are private and non-profit US healthcare providers (physician groups, health systems, hospitals). No Indian or US government direct contract exposure.

rate_sensitive.evidence: AQuity acquisition debt ~₹856 Cr as of March 2025, USD-denominated from global banks (JPMorgan, Citi, HSBC), likely SOFR-linked (floating rate). TruBridge acquisition facility (announced April 2026) at SOFR + 275 bps. Exact floating vs fixed split not explicitly disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No systematic forex hedging found; company relies on natural hedge from INR cost base vs USD revenue, with partial offset from USD-denominated AQuity acquisition debt.
inr_exposure.evidence: US clients = ~96% of consolidated FY25 revenue (₹2,664 Cr total); Canada and Australia = ~4%. IPO RHP confirms standalone India entity: US revenue = 99.94% of revenue in FY24 (pre-AQuity consolidation).

pli_scheme.evidence: Healthcare IT services company; PLI schemes are for manufacturing sectors. Company previously benefited from SEIS (Service Exports from India Scheme) as a SEEPZ-SEZ unit.

rural.evidence: Pan-India sales network reaching over 60,000 retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration. Regular category IMFL volume = 53.9% of total IMFL volumes, primarily distributed through mass-market channels including rural outlets. No specific rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~Rs. 750-1,000 Cr (long-term ~Rs. 200 Cr + working capital ~Rs. 693 Cr); Debt/Equity = 0.10-0.36x; working capital borrowings in India typically on floating MCLR-linked rates. Exact floating rate % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~8-9% of net revenue, primarily USD/GBP/EUR (Rampur Single Malt in ~50 countries, Jaisalmer Gin in ~40 countries + travel retail). Hedging policy not disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: IMFL/spirits are explicitly excluded from all PLI schemes.

govt_capex.evidence: Mobility segment (~22% of Q4 FY2025 revenue at ₹1,135 Cr) is almost entirely Indian Railways/government exposure, including ₹13,000 crore locomotive contract. Smart Infrastructure (~53% of Q4 FY2025 revenue at ₹2,725 Cr) includes state electricity utilities (government) and commercial buildings (private). Combined government/PSU-linked revenue estimated at 40-55% of total but not separately disclosed. FY2024-25 full-year revenue ₹17,364 Cr (post Energy demerger, continuing operations). Note: Energy segment demerged into Siemens Energy India Limited effective March 2025.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Siemens India is a net cash / zero debt company. No long-term external borrowings. Floating rate liability not applicable.

crude_exposure.evidence: Capital goods manufacturer; primary raw materials are copper, steel, aluminum, and electronic components. Minimal direct crude oil exposure.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Forward exchange contracts to hedge firm commitments and forecast transactions, up to 12-month horizon; cash flow hedges under Ind AS 109.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenues ~7-10% of total FY2024-25 revenue (₹17,364 Cr continuing operations). Exports primarily through Siemens global supply chain (switchgear, transformers, drives). Note: FY2024-25 = Oct 2024 – Sep 2025 (Siemens India's October fiscal year-end).

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI beneficiary status confirmed for Siemens India as of FY2024-25. Revenue is largely through project/systems integration rather than product manufacturing qualifying for PLI.

rural.evidence: B30 (Beyond Top 30 cities) AUM = Rs 1.32 lakh crore = ~19.8% of total MF AUM vs industry average 18.6%. 70% of NAM India's branches are in B30 locations. Manages government-backed POLI (Post Office Life Insurance) and RPOLI (Rural Post Office Life Insurance) mandates. 20.8 million unique investors, largest in industry.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is completely debt-free (Borrowings = INR 0 for FY25 per Motilal Oswal balance sheet; consistent FY20-FY25). Zero interest-bearing liabilities. Primary revenue driver is AUM level driven by equity market performance, not interest rates directly.

inr_exposure.evidence: Offshore Business + GIFT City AUM = ₹15,246 crore (~2.7% of total MF QAAUM) managed via Singapore subsidiary (NAM Singapore). UCITS flagship fund ~USD 543 million. USD advisory fee income estimated ~2-3% of consolidated revenue. No formal hedging policy; amounts are immaterial.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI schemes are for manufacturing sectors; AMCs are not eligible.

china_plus_one.evidence: AR FY2024-25 (p.47): 'While continuing to strengthen its market share in Western regions, Sona Comstar is intensifying its focus on Eastern markets to tap into both automotive and non-automotive mobility opportunities.' Company entered JV with Jinnaite Machinery Co. (China) for driveline systems — actively entering, not exiting China. No China+1 language in FY2024-25 AR.

govt_capex.evidence: Commercial vehicles segment (~11% of FY25 revenue) has indirect government infra capex linkage. Acquired Escorts Kubota Railway Equipment Division (closed June 2025, post FY25) adding direct railway government capex exposure. AR: 'With the increasing capex and budgetary support from the government for expanding the railway network... the railway component market in India offers a significant opportunity.'

rate_sensitive.evidence: Variable rate borrowings as at March 31, 2025: INR 134.63 million only (WCDL from Citi Bank China at 1Y LPR + 100 bps). Company net-debt free with net cash of INR 26,591 million consolidated. Interest rate sensitivity of ±1% = INR 9.22 million PAT impact — negligible.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are special steel alloy bars, iron castings, steel blanks — not directly crude-linked. Material cost = 43% of total income (both FY2024-25 and FY2023-24) per AR MD&A expenditure breakup.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy using forward contracts. USD forward contracts receivable: USD 109.55 million (INR 9,452 Cr) as at March 31, 2025. EUR forward contracts receivable: EUR 20.81 million. Hedge accounting applied under Ind AS 109.
inr_exposure.evidence: AR MD&A: North America = 41% of total FY2024-25 revenue; Europe = 24%; Asia (excl. India) = 6%; rest ~0.3%. Total exports = 71% of revenue. Note: 'North America' reported as a unit; no US-only split provided.

pli_scheme.evidence: AR Board's Report: 'your Company has received certifications for more products i.e. Traction Motor for electric three-wheelers, Hub Wheel Integrated Motor for electric two-wheelers under the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry.' CFO Review: 'We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved.'
